changes.before: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent.
The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run.
changes.after: The Committee's two percent longer-run inflation goal was not a focus of the review.

The updated statement, also commonly known as the consensus statement, emphasizes that the FOMC's monetary policy strategy is designed to promote the congressionally-assigned goals of maximum employment and stable prices across a broad range of economic conditions for the benefit and well-being of all Americans.

changes.before: Voting against this action were Michelle W. Bowman and Christopher J. Waller, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.
changes.after: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Friday announced the unanimous approval of updates to its Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy

parsed.rationale: The current document is a framework-review announcement rather than a policy statement, and it contains no assessment of the economy, rate decision, or forward guidance. It reaffirms the 2 percent goal and the dual mandate without signaling any change in the near-term policy stance.

spans.quote: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent.
The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run.
Voting against this action were Michelle W. Bowman and Christopher J. Waller, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.
The Committee's two percent longer-run inflation goal was not a focus of the review.

The updated statement, also commonly known as the consensus statement, emphasizes that the FOMC's monetary policy strategy is designed to promote the congressionally-assigned goals of maximum employment and stable prices across a broad range of economic conditions for the benefit and well-being of all Americans.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Friday announced the unanimous approval of updates to its Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy
